# Core lib scan — noteworthy findings

Scan date: 2026-08-19. Scope: all of `libs/core` — about 15.9k lines of non-spec source under
`src/`, plus about 6.3k lines across the six Nx generators, the packaging files, the stories,
and the 15 docs pages under `apps/docs/core`. Seven parallel review agents read the source.
Each agent verified its claims against the code, and each verified its top claims at runtime.

Severity counts: **29 high**, **68 medium**, **~60 low**.

## Summary of the worst problems

1. Every shortcut SEO binding (`applyDescriptionBinding`, `applyCanonicalBinding`, `applyOpenGraphBindings`, and eleven more) is dead to signal changes: an `untracked` read inside the wrapper computed strips all dependencies, so the tag neither updates nor gets removed. The docs promise the opposite. (seo)
2. Two XSS sinks: `StructuredDataComponent`'s hand-rolled `</script>` escape is bypassed by `</SCRIPT >`, and `markdownToHtml` accepts an entity-encoded `javascript:` URL that the browser decodes into a live scheme. Both were exploited at runtime. (seo, utils)
3. A modal overlay's focus trap only listens on the pane, so once focus leaves the pane (backdrop click, `autoFocus: false`), Tab walks into the page behind the modal. (overlay)
4. The first overlay mount in a document deletes every `.et-overlay-runtime-root`, including live roots owned by another Angular app on the same page. (overlay)
5. Every `[etAnimatedLifecycle]` instance — so every overlay pane — runs a self-perpetuating `requestAnimationFrame` loop for its whole lifetime, just to hold a frame counter. (animations)
6. The breakpoint input transforms (`numberBreakpointTransform` and friends) return the raw map object when no key matches the current breakpoint, because the transform captures the first bound value as its own fallback. (signals)
7. The element-signal helpers construct `ResizeObserver`/`MutationObserver` eagerly and read required inputs eagerly, so they crash on the server and throw NG0950 on required inputs — both against documented usage. (signals)
8. Small utilities with wrong core behavior: `normalizeMatchState` has an inverted branch and misclassifies every input, `IsEmail` rejects all uppercase addresses, `cloneFormGroup` throws on any disabled control, and `getCookie` returns `''` for a missing cookie. (utils, pipes)
9. Lifetime leaks: `injectAngularRootElement` polls `setTimeout` forever when no root component mounts, and `signalAnimatedNumber` keeps its rAF loop running after the component is destroyed. (providers, signals)
10. The `migrate-to-v5` generator corrupts realistic consumer workspaces in at least ten verified ways — stale splice offsets mangle a second component in a file, `[theme]` → `[color]` rewrites every unrelated binding in the workspace, a consumer's own `RouterStateService` is hijacked, and the color renames target class names that do not exist in v5. (generator)
11. `migrate-provider-shape` matches factories by identifier name only, so a workspace's own `createProvider`/`createLabels` helper is rewritten into imports that do not resolve; the tailwind generators can overwrite a hand-written stylesheet via the `.d.ts` path derivation and silently drop `interactionColor` swatches. (generators)
12. The only three component stylesheets in `libs/core` (the two theming interactive sheets and the inline resize-handles styles) are the only shipped component CSS in the repo not wrapped in `@layer components`, which inverts the documented override model. (theming, resize-handles)

---

## signals

### High

- **`breakpointTransformBase` uses the first _bound_ value as the map fallback, so a map with no key at/below the current breakpoint resolves to the raw map object.** `breakpoint-input.ts:70-73` captures `capturedDefault = coerced as T` from the first transform invocation — and Angular never calls a transform with the input's declared default, so for the normal case (`[columns]="{ md: 3 }"`) `capturedDefault` _is_ the map. `resolveFromMap` (`breakpoint-input.ts:47-54`) then returns it as the value (`breakpoint-input.ts:75-77`, and again on every breakpoint change at `:97`). The same object is what the docs say produces `[object Object]` (`apps/docs/core/signal-utils.md:49-51`) — except that warning is only about _invalid_ keys. Verified at runtime: `columns = input(1, { transform: numberBreakpointTransform() })` bound to `{ md: 3 }` under jsdom (all media queries false → breakpoint `xs`) yields `typeof columns() = object`, `value = {"md":3}` — not `1`. `injectBreakpointInput(signal, defaultValue)` (`:144`) takes an explicit default and is correct; only the transform factories are broken.
- **Passing a required input signal to any element-signal helper throws NG0950 at construction.** `buildElementSignal` → `isElementSignal` reads the signal eagerly to sniff its shape (`element.ts:41-46`, called at `element.ts:78`), so `signalElementMutations(this.someRequiredInput)` in a field initializer explodes before the input is set. `apps/docs/core/element-signals.md:23-24` explicitly documents both halves of that usage ("call the helpers in a constructor or field initializer" + "a signal/observable of any of them"). The rest of the lib already guards this exact case (`control-value.ts:25-32`, `signal-data-utils.ts:44-56`), so the pattern is known. Verified at runtime: `Error: NG0950: Input is required but no value is available yet.`
- **`signalAnimatedNumber` never cancels its animation frame loop on destroy — the rAF chain and `onAnimationEnd` keep firing after the component is gone.** `animated-number.ts:83-141` stores `rafId` and defines `cancelAnimation()` (`:86`), but nothing hooks `DestroyRef`; only the caller calling `.stop()`/`.reset()` cancels it, and `ngZone.run(() => options.onAnimationEnd?.())` (`:131-133`) runs on a destroyed context. Verified at runtime: with a component created, `.play()`ed and then `fixture.destroy()`ed, the signal continued to advance from `183` to `834` over the next 500 ms.
- **The element helpers construct browser observers eagerly, so they crash in any non-browser environment — directly contradicting the docs' "SSR-safe" claim.** `apps/docs/core/element-signals.md:25` states "**SSR-safe** - the observers only attach after first render (`signalIsRendered()`)". In reality `signalIsRendered()` only gates the observer _callback_: `new ResizeObserver(...)` runs at call time in `element-dimensions.ts:94` and `animated-block-size.ts:148`, `new MutationObserver(...)` at `element-mutations.ts:14`, plus bare `getComputedStyle` at `element-dimensions.ts:118` and `media-queries.ts:134`, and bare `requestAnimationFrame` via `nextFrame` in `render-utils.ts:15,32` (the two "render guards" the same doc section lists). `signalElementScrollState`/`signalElementChildren`/`useCursorDragScroll` all inherit it. Verified at runtime: `signalElementDimensions(document.createElement('div'))` in an env without `ResizeObserver` throws `ReferenceError: ResizeObserver is not defined` at the call, not at render. (`signalElementIntersection` is the one that genuinely is guarded — `element-intersection.ts:104-113` constructs only once `rendered` is true.)

### Medium

- **Forgetting `provideBreakpointInstance` doesn't degrade the transform, it kills the component.** `breakpoint-input.ts:85` does `injector.get(BREAKPOINT_INSTANCE_TOKEN)` with no default inside the effect, for _every_ value including plain non-map ones. Verified at runtime: `ɵNotFound: NG0201: No provider found for InjectionToken BREAKPOINT_INSTANCE_TOKEN` thrown out of the first change detection. `apps/docs/core/signal-utils.md:47` only says the provider "is required for the transforms to re-resolve when the breakpoint changes", which reads as a reactivity opt-in. The lookup itself is also fragile: it enumerates the instance's own keys and matches on `[SIGNAL].transformFn` identity (`breakpoint-input.ts:86-93`).
- **`controlValueSignal`'s `debounceFirst` option does nothing.** `control-value.ts:48-50` puts `startWith(ctrl.getRawValue())` _after_ `debounceTime`, and `toSignal` is given `initialValue` anyway (`:57-59`), so the initial value always lands synchronously whether or not the `merge(of(initialValue), …)` branch is taken (`:55`). Verified at runtime: with `{ debounceTime: 100, debounceFirst: true }` vs `false`, both signals read `'a'` immediately. Documented as a real option in `apps/docs/core/signal-utils.md:81`.
- **`syncSignal`'s `skipFirstRun` is silently ignored when `skipSyncRead` is true.** `signal-data-utils.ts:42` initializes `isFirstRun = options?.skipSyncRead ? false : true`, so the `skipFirstRun` branch at `:61-65` can never trigger for the one combination that would need it (a required input you want to sync but not clobber on the first flush). `apps/docs/core/signal-utils.md:137` presents the two options as independent. Verified at runtime: `syncSignal(from, to, { skipSyncRead: true, skipFirstRun: true })` wrote `1` into `to` on the first flush.
- **`createRoute(router)` touches `window` with no platform guard.** `router.ts:154` — public, exported, and recommended for "synchronous, non-injected use inside `router.events` handlers" (`apps/docs/core/signal-utils.md:73`). Its sibling `createInitialRoute` does guard (`router.ts:43-50`) and `injectQueryParam`'s helper uses a `typeof window` check (`router.ts:230`), so this one is an outlier. The only in-repo caller happens to be behind a browser check (`recipes/scroll-restoration.ts:199`), so it's the public surface that is exposed.
- **`InjectUtilConfig.injector` is dead config.** `router.ts:18-21` documents "Must be provided if the function is not called from within a injection context", and the only consumer is `injectFragment` (`router.ts:177-183`), which never reads `config.injector` — it calls `injectRouterState()` directly and therefore still requires an injection context.
- **The CSS-var writers latch on a module-level flag, so a second app instance (or anything after teardown) silently never gets the variables.** `recipes/css-vars.ts:6,18-21` and `:39,51-54` set `hasWritten*` before creating the effect and never reset it. Destroy the injector that called it (HMR, tests, a second `bootstrapApplication` on the same page) and `--et-sw`/`--et-sh`/`--et-vw`/`--et-vh` are never written or updated again. Docs sell this as "idempotent" (`apps/docs/core/signal-utils.md:150`), which is only true for one app lifetime.
- **A pending scroll restoration is not cleaned up on destroy.** `recipes/scroll-restoration.ts:296-323` registers three capture-phase `document` listeners and a rAF loop, and `pendingRestore` is only invoked from `cancelPendingRestore` on a new navigation or on completion (`:239-242`). `takeUntilDestroyed()` at `:467` stops the router subscription but nothing calls `cancelPendingRestore` on destroy, so the loop and the listeners outlive the injector (up to `maxTimeout`, default 10 s) and can still write `scrollTop` on a detached page.
- **`navigationId` 0 doubles as the "no restored state" sentinel in scroll restoration.** `recipes/scroll-restoration.ts:230` starts `lastNavigationId = 0` and `:354-359` stores a real offset under key `0` at the first `NavigationStart`; `:368` falls back to `0` when a popstate carries no `restoredState`, and `:400-409` then restores `positions.get(0)` with no route check. A popstate over a history entry Angular didn't create restores the offset of the pre-first-navigation page.
- **`signalElementIntersection` keeps stale entries when it is disabled.** `element-intersection.ts:100-116` disconnects and sets `observer` to `null` when `enabled` flips false, but the second effect's `updateObservedElements` returns early on a null observer (`:121`) without clearing `elementIntersectionSignal`, so consumers keep reading the last known intersection state as if it were current.
- **`injectScrollbarDimensions` appends a measuring `<div>` to `document.body` and never removes it.** `media-queries.ts:128-137` — no `DestroyRef.onDestroy`, and the signal is memoized per environment injector, so the ruler outlives the app that created it.
- **`injectViewportSize` is the one `inject*` helper that is not memoized.** `element-dimensions.ts:141-167` adds a `visualViewport`/`window` resize listener per call site (cleaned up on destroy, but never shared), while every sibling helper goes through `memoizeSignal` (`media-queries.ts:14-121`) and the `rxjs-signals` skill tells consumers to reach for it by default.

### Low

- Unreachable error path: `element-intersection.ts:145-152` warns "No visibility data found for element" but `isElementVisible` only returns `null` for a falsy `element` (`scrolling/scrollable.ts:121-123`), and the loop iterates non-null elements.
- `element-intersection.ts:110-113` spreads the whole options object into `IntersectionObserverInit`, passing the `enabled` signal function as an unknown init key.
- Dead truthiness checks on an always-present injected renderer: `animated-block-size.ts:105,134`.
- Comment-policy violations: `animated-number.ts:104` ("// Skip animation if no change" over `if (delta === 0)`); `recipes/cursor-drag-scroll.ts:76,85,133` (narration headers over each effect); `recipes/cursor-drag-scroll.ts:53` and `animated-block-size.ts:168` (repeat what the adjacent JSDoc already says); the identical two-line "we are not interested what the mutation is" block duplicated at `element-children.ts:33-34` and `element-scroll-state.ts:77-78`.
- `element-dimensions.ts:1` imports `DOCUMENT` from `@angular/common` while every other file in the dir imports it from `@angular/core` (`element.ts:1`, `media-queries.ts:1`, `recipes/cursor-drag-scroll.ts:1`).
- Exported-but-unused/undocumented API: `booleanBreakpointAttribute` / `numberBreakpointAttribute` (`breakpoint-input.ts:154-162`, zero consumers anywhere, absent from the docs), `breakpointTransformBase` (`:56`, low-level, undocumented), `areScrollStatesEqual` (`element-scroll-state.ts:32`, only used internally).
- `control-value.ts:69`'s `T extends Signal<infer TSignalControl>` branch is unreachable — `controlValueSignalWithPrevious` constrains `T extends AbstractControl`, so unlike `controlValueSignal` it cannot take a signal at all.
- `takeUntilDestroyed` is not last in the pipe at `recipes/cursor-drag-scroll.ts:205-208` (the `rxjs-signals` skill asks for the limiting operator last).
- `subscribe()` with a body at `deferred-loading.ts:61-67` and `recipes/scroll-restoration.ts:469-477` — `ethlete/no-subscribe-with-body` exists but is explicitly disabled for this lib (`libs/core/eslint.config.mjs:87`), so these are pre-existing backlog, not new violations.
- `recipes/scroll-restoration.ts:254` computes the hard deadline as `Math.max(restoreTimeout, restoreMaxTimeout)`, so a `maxTimeout` smaller than `timeout` is ignored despite being documented as an "absolute upper bound" (`:36-41`).
- Doc gaps (not contradictions): `signalElementChildren`'s `mutations` option (`element-children.ts:6-17`) and `useCursorDragScroll`'s `canScroll` option (`recipes/cursor-drag-scroll.ts:18-26`) are undocumented; `apps/docs/core/signal-utils.md:21` calls `injectScrollbarDimensions` "measured once" though it is `ResizeObserver`-backed and live.

Clean: subscription hygiene is good in the RxJS-using files — `element-scroll-direction.ts:53`, `deferred-loading.ts:59`, `recipes/cursor-drag-scroll.ts:205,214,232` and `recipes/scroll-restoration.ts:467` all terminate with `takeUntilDestroyed`, and the three observer-based helpers (`element-dimensions.ts:132`, `element-mutations.ts:38`, `element-intersection.ts:198`) disconnect on destroy. No `.subscribe()`-and-assign anywhere; the signal↔RxJS boundary is crossed with `toSignal`/`toObservable` throughout, and no RxJS is created inside an `effect`/`computed`. `deferred-loading.ts` is correct on every path traced (delay swallow, min-duration hold, re-show cancelling a pending hide, server no-op) and matches its docs exactly. `router.ts`'s committed-URL logic (`:91-111`) does what its comments and the docs claim, including the pre-first-navigation fallback, and `injectRouterNavigationState` matches its JSDoc. `memoizeSignal`'s per-`EnvironmentInjector` `WeakMap` (`signal-data-utils.ts:137-151`) is sound and matches the docs' claim. `scroll-restoration`'s hold registry, position-eviction cap and query-param matching are all consistent with their docs. Most option defaults cross-checked against both doc tables (`animated-block-size` 160/`ease`/`['block']`, `signalAnimatedNumber` 1000/`easeOut`/`Math.round`, `signalDeferredLoading` 200/300, restore 1000/10000/`clampOnTimeout: true`) are accurate.

### Spec coverage

- Covered well: `recipes/scroll-restoration.spec.ts` (411 lines, 15 cases — popstate restore, clamp/no-clamp, holds, user-scroll abort, supersede, marked navigations, query-param matching, `routerDisableScrollTop`) and `deferred-loading.spec.ts` (6 cases with fake timers covering every branch). `router.spec.ts` covers the constructor-timing behavior of `injectRoute`/`injectUrl`/`injectPathParam`/`injectQueryParam`/`injectRouteDataItem`, and documents the `memoizeSignal`-cache-vs-TestBed hazard.
- Zero tests, all carrying real logic: `element.ts` (the whole binding-coercion matrix — `QueryList`, arrays, observables, the `isElementSignal` sniff that throws on required inputs), `element-dimensions.ts`, `element-mutations.ts`, `element-children.ts`, `element-intersection.ts`, `element-scroll-state.ts`, `element-scroll-direction.ts`, `element-data-binding.ts` (six public binding helpers plus `buildSignalEffects`' push/remove lifecycle), `breakpoint-input.ts` (where both High/Medium findings live), `animated-number.ts`, `animated-block-size.ts`, `control-value.ts`, `signal-data-utils.ts`, `media-queries.ts`, `render-utils.ts`, `recipes/cursor-drag-scroll.ts`, `recipes/css-vars.ts`. That is ~2.6k of the ~3.2k non-spec lines untested.
- The observer-based helpers are effectively untestable in the current setup as written: `libs/core/vite.config.mts` uses `environment: 'jsdom'` and `src/test-setup.ts` adds no `ResizeObserver`/`IntersectionObserver` polyfill, so any spec touching `signalElementDimensions` (and therefore `signalElementScrollState`, `injectViewportDimensions`, `injectScrollbarDimensions`, `useCursorDragScroll`, `injectAnimatedBlockSize`) throws at the call. That absence is also what makes the "SSR-safe" doc claim easy to verify as wrong.
- No spec encodes a wrong behavior: none of the existing tests assert any of the defects above (the buggy paths simply have no tests).

## overlay, animations, scrolling

### High

- **A modal overlay's focus trap is escapable: the `keydown` handler is bound to the pane, so when focus is not inside the pane, Tab walks straight into the page behind the modal.**
  `setupFocusTrap` attaches to `paneElement` only (`libs/core/src/lib/overlay/overlay-focus.ts:117`), so it never sees a Tab press whose target is outside the pane. Focus legitimately sits outside in plausible configs: `autoFocus: false` with `modal: true` (a type-legal combination), or after the user clicks the backdrop/host of a modal (a non-focusable element blurs the active element to `<body>`; a modal's `closeOnOutsidePointer` defaults to `false`, `libs/core/src/lib/overlay/overlay-runtime.ts:371`). No other focus trap exists in the SDK — `libs/components` only reuses `applyInitialFocus`/`getFocusableElements`, never `setupFocusTrap`. Verified at runtime (jsdom): with `modal: true, autoFocus: false` and focus on a button outside the pane — `activeElement inside pane? false`, `Tab defaultPrevented by trap? false`.
- **An in-flight `computePosition` from the anchored strategy resolves after cleanup and stamps anchored position styles onto a pane that has already been re-positioned (or is animating out).**
  `libs/core/src/lib/overlay/overlay-position-anchored.ts:296-326` writes `transform`, `width`, `visibility`, `--et-overlay-anchored-x/y` and `data-overlay-placement` in a `.then()` with no cancellation flag; the cleanup returned at `:334` only stops `autoUpdate` and the inset listener. `overlayRef.updatePositionStrategy()` (`overlay-runtime.ts:244-255`) runs `positionCleanup()` → `resetPositioningStyles()` → new setup synchronously, so the pending promise lands afterwards. This is exactly the documented responsive dialog↔bottom-sheet morph path (`apps/docs/core/overlay-runtime.md:133`). Verified at runtime: mount anchored → `updatePositionStrategy({ kind: 'center' })` → after microtasks the centered pane carries `transform: "translate3d(100px, 192px, 0)"`, `data-overlay-placement="top"`, `--et-overlay-anchored-x: "100px"` — i.e. a centered dialog rendered offset by the old anchor delta.
- **The runtime's first mount in a document deletes every `.et-overlay-runtime-root` in that document, including live roots owned by another Angular app on the page.**
  `libs/core/src/lib/overlay/overlay-runtime.ts:63` runs `targetDocument.querySelectorAll('.et-overlay-runtime-root').forEach((el) => el.remove())` whenever `rootElements` has no entry for the document — which is true for a second app's root-provided runtime, and again for any runtime after all of its overlays closed (`maybeDestroyRootElements` drops the map entry at `:114-116`). The victim runtime is never told: its `openEntriesState` still lists the entries, their `hostElement`s are now detached, and their leave animations/teardown never run. Reachable wherever two Angular apps share a document (Storybook docs pages rendering several stories, micro-frontends) — the very scenario the comment cites as the motivation. Verified at runtime: a foreign `.et-overlay-runtime-root` placed in `<body>` is `isConnected === false` immediately after the first `mount()`.
- **Every `AnimatedLifecycleDirective` instance runs a self-perpetuating `requestAnimationFrame` loop for its entire lifetime, purely to hold a frame counter.**
  `libs/core/src/lib/animations/animated-lifecycle.directive.ts:81-90`: `updateFrameId` re-arms itself unconditionally from the constructor, and is only cancelled in `DestroyRef.onDestroy`. Its sole consumer is the `forcedAtFrameId === currentFrameId` same-frame check at `:122` and `:211`. Consequence: as long as any element carries `[etAnimatedLifecycle]` (every overlay pane, plus form-field/menu/tooltip internals in `libs/components`), the page's frame loop never idles, and the cost is N callbacks per frame for N mounted instances — permanent main-thread/battery cost with nothing animating. A monotonic counter driven off the existing transition plumbing, or a single shared frame ticker, would remove it.

### Medium

- **Escape is swallowed while the top-most overlay plays its leave animation.** `isTopMost` compares against `openEntriesState().at(-1)` (`overlay-runtime.ts:119-121`), and an entry stays in `openEntries` until `destroyMountedOverlay` runs after the lifecycle reaches `'left'` (`:340-348`). So during the leave transition the closing overlay is still "top-most" — its own `close()` returns early (`overlay-runtime-ref.ts:43-45`) and the overlay beneath it refuses to handle the key. Verified at runtime: bottom + top overlay mounted; `top.close()` → `top.state() === 'closing'`; a document `keydown` Escape leaves `bottom.state() === 'mounted'`. Two quick Escape presses therefore close one overlay, not two.
- **The anchored `flip` middleware ignores `strategy.viewportPadding`, while `shift` and `size` honour it.** `overlay-position-anchored.ts:221` passes `padding: insets` (reservations only), whereas `:242` and `:256` pass `paddingWithInsets(strategy.viewportPadding ?? 8, insets)`. A pane therefore decides whether to flip using 0 viewport padding but is shifted/capped using 8px (or the caller's value) — it can flip to a side where `size` then caps it more tightly than the flip decision assumed. `apps/docs/core/overlay-runtime.md:94` states the reserved edge behaves "exactly as it does against the viewport edge" for flip/shift/autoResize, which only holds for the reservation half.
- **`createFlipAnimation().cancel()` can never emit `onCancel$`, and repeated `play()` calls accumulate `fill: 'both'` animations on the element.** `libs/core/src/lib/animations/flip-animation.ts:185-189` calls `animation.cancel()` and then `cleanup()` synchronously; the `cancel` event is queued as a task, so the listener registered at `:180` is already gone when it fires. Verified at runtime with a spec-faithful fake Animation (async `cancel` dispatch): `onCancel$` emissions after `cancel()` = 0. Separately, `play()` (`:158`) creates a new `Animation` with `fill: 'both'` without cancelling the previous one and `cleanup()` never cancels or removes the finished animation, so N `play()` calls leave N filling animations retained by the element.
- **`apps/docs/core/animations.md:3` claims "There is no built-in reduced-motion handling" — there is.** `flip-animation.ts:156` collapses the duration to 0 under `matchesReducedMotion(el)`, `ignoreReducedMotion` opts out (`:30`, `:101`), and `matchesReducedMotion()` is exported (`animations/index.ts:5`, `animation-utils.ts:34`). The FLIP section (`animations.md:82`) lists the config as `{ element, originElement?, duration?, easing? }` and omits `ignoreReducedMotion` entirely; `matchesReducedMotion` appears nowhere in `apps/docs` (it is announced in `libs/core/CHANGELOG.md:246`).
- **The interrupt-class descriptions in the Storybook docs are swapped.** `libs/core/src/lib/animations/animated-lifecycle.directive.docs.mdx:77-78` says `et-animation-enter-interrupt` = "Enter interrupted by leave" and `et-animation-leave-interrupt` = the reverse. In the code, `enterInterrupt` is added by `enter()` when it interrupts a _leave_ (`animated-lifecycle.directive.ts:148-156`) and `leaveInterrupt` by `leave()` interrupting an _enter_ (`:237-245`).
- **`isElementVisible` reports full visibility for any element whenever the container cannot scroll, without looking at geometry.** `libs/core/src/lib/scrolling/scrollable.ts:128-142` short-circuits to `isIntersecting: true, intersectionRatio: 1` on `!elementCanScroll(container)`. With no `container` that check is against `document.documentElement`, so on any page without a document scrollbar the function reports every element — including one far outside the viewport — as fully visible. `apps/docs/core/scrolling.md:32` documents it as "how visible an element is inside a container (or the viewport)" with no mention of the short-circuit.
- **Doc/code signature and enum mismatches in `apps/docs/core/overlay-runtime.md`.** `:147` lists the close sources as `'api' | 'escape' | 'outside-pointer' | 'drag'`, omitting `'reference-detached'`, which is in the type (`overlay-runtime.types.ts:9`) and discussed 6 lines later at `:153`. `:161` documents `isFocusable(el)`; the real signature is `isFocusable(element, document)` (`overlay-focus.ts:20`) and callers must pass the document (`libs/components/src/lib/forms/form/focus-first-invalid-field.ts:78`). The `document` mount option (`overlay-runtime.types.ts:152`) is missing from the mount-config table.
- **Synchronous state is modelled with subjects on public animation API.** `animated-lifecycle.directive.ts:58` `state$ = new BehaviorSubject<AnimatedLifecycleState>('init')` is read synchronously as `.value` by its own `enter()`/`leave()` (`:97`, `:187`) and by the runtime (`overlay-runtime.ts:323`, `:440`); `animatable.directive.ts:41-42` keeps `activeAnimationCount` in a plain field and copies it into `hostActiveAnimationCount$` on every change (`:168-174`). Both are exactly what `.agents/skills/rxjs-signals/SKILL.md` forbids ("Synchronous state → signals. Never model sync state with a `BehaviorSubject`/`Subject`", "Bridge, don't copy"). It is public API, so the fix is a breaking rename/bridge, but it is worth recording rather than being read as the house pattern.
- **`OverlayRuntimeRef` hands consumers the runtime's own mutators with no `@internal` marking.** `overlay-runtime-ref.ts` exposes `beforeOpenedSubject` (`:40`, marked internal in a plain comment only), `attachComponentRef` (`:89`), `markOpened` (`:123`), `beginClose` (`:133`) and `finishClose` (`:145`) as public members of the object every `mount()` returns, while `attachPositionUpdater`/`attachBackdropUpdater` (`:93`, `:106`) do carry `@internal`. A consumer calling `finishClose()` flips `state` to `'closed'` and completes `afterClosed()` while the DOM, listeners and component ref stay alive. None of them are in the ref table at `apps/docs/core/overlay-runtime.md:139-149`.
- **`applyInitialFocus` passes a caller-supplied string straight to `querySelector` with no guard.** `overlay-focus.ts:73`; `autoFocus` is typed `OverlayRuntimeAutoFocusTarget | string | false` (`overlay-runtime.types.ts:131`), so any non-selector string (or a malformed one) throws `SyntaxError` from inside the enter-frame callback (`overlay-runtime.ts:432`, `:467`), where nothing catches it — the overlay is left mounted but never reaches `'mounted'`.
- **`config.providers` cannot accept `EnvironmentProviders`, and the mounted component does not get the caller's environment injector.** `overlay-runtime.types.ts:126` types it `StaticProvider[]` and `overlay-runtime.ts:207-210` builds it with `Injector.create({...}) as EnvironmentInjector` (a cast to reach `.destroyed`/`.destroy()`), then passes the runtime's own `environmentInjector` to `createComponent` (`:212-217`) while `config.injector` only reaches the element injector's parent chain. So `provideX()`-style features cannot be passed at all, and an overlay opened from a route-scoped environment resolves environment-level DI against the root.
- **Unguarded `console.warn` in library code.** `animatable.directive.ts:123-125` warns on every stray `animationend`/`transitioncancel` (e.g. an animation that began before the directive existed) with no `isDevMode()` gate, unlike the sibling diagnostics at `overlay-position.ts:179` and `overlay-position-anchored.ts:50`.

### Low

- `openEntries = computed(() => openEntriesState())` (`overlay-runtime.ts:42`) is a no-op wrapper where `openEntriesState.asReadonly()` says the same thing.
- App-teardown path calls `destroyMountedOverlay` directly (`overlay-runtime.ts:310`), skipping `beginClose`, so `beforeClosed()` never emits and `state` jumps `'mounted' → 'closed'`.
- `resetPositioningStyles` (`overlay-position.ts:106-138`) clears `--et-overlay-anchored-*` but not the arrow's `--et-floating-arrow-translate` (set at `overlay-position-anchored.ts:320`), so a stale arrow offset survives a strategy swap.
- `animated-if.directive.ts:47-53` subscribes to `state$` filtered on `'left'` without `take(1)`, so a later `forceLeftState()` re-runs `viewContainerRef.clear()` on an already-cleared container.
- `libs/core/src/lib/animations/flip-animation.docs.mdx` and `animation-utils.docs.mdx` are title-only stubs (5 lines each) shipped as Storybook doc pages.
- Comment policy (`AGENTS.md`, "Comments: almost none"): `overlay-runtime.ts:201-202` is migration narration that also restates the code below it ("matches the previous overlay behavior…"); `animation-utils.ts:19-21` and `scrollable.ts:4-6`/`:24-27` are rationale for a mechanical choice (a guarded lazy fallback), repeated at three sites; `overlay-position.ts:12-15` and `overlay-position-anchored.ts:142-145` are JSDoc on non-exported helpers. The bulk of the remaining comments in these files do land inside the allowlist (ordering constraints like `overlay-runtime.ts:219-220` and `overlay-position-anchored.ts:248-249`, and the `preferredSide` invariant).
- `setupScrollRestoration` sets `history.scrollRestoration = 'manual'` (`signals/recipes/scroll-restoration.ts:221-223`) and never restores it, so the setting outlives the app within the document.

Clean: the stacking-level and viewport-reservation subsystems are the strongest part of this scope — `resolveOverlayLayer`/`isOnHigherOverlayLayer` handle null, non-`Element` and unparsable-attribute inputs, reservations are max-per-edge and layer-scoped exactly as documented, the published `--et-viewport-inset-*` properties are removed when the last reservation is released, and `globalThis.document?.documentElement` keeps it SSR-safe. Overlay teardown is careful in the ways that usually go wrong: every listener/observer/subscription is registered into `cleanupFns`, the element injector is explicitly destroyed so overlay-scoped `DestroyRef` hooks run, `mountedTeardowns` gives a synchronous bypass for app teardown mid-animation, and the enter frame bails out when the state moved on. `whenAnimationsSettled` correctly re-reads `getAnimations()` (retargeted transitions), filters endless and pseudo-element animations, uses `allSettled` so a cancelled animation cannot strand a transition, and deliberately defers the first-read emission off the `enter()`/`leave()` stack. `capture`/`passive` listener hygiene and add/remove option symmetry are right everywhere checked, including the scroll-restoration interaction listeners. SSR guards are present in `forceReflow`, `matchesReducedMotion`, `elementCanScroll`, `createViewportRect` and `publishInsetProperties`. No CSS ships in this scope, so the `@layer components` and hardcoded-colour rules do not apply; `snap.ts` and `scrollable.ts` are pure, side-effect-free geometry with no framework coupling. The `scroll-restoration.md` page is unusually accurate — it even documents the `max(timeout, maxTimeout)` quirk and the scrollbar-drag gap.

### Spec coverage

- **`scrolling/` has zero spec files** — 516 lines of pure, trivially testable geometry (`snap.ts`'s oversized-item and `origin: 'auto'` branches, `getScrollItemTarget`'s six-way index logic, `getElementScrollCoordinates`'s four origins) is entirely untested. Biggest gap in the scope.
- **`overlay-focus.ts` has no spec** — the focus trap, `applyInitialFocus`'s five modes and `isFocusable`'s visibility filter carry all the a11y behaviour and none of the tests. (jsdom's `getClientRects()` always returns 0, so `getFocusableElements` needs stubbing — which is why the runtime spec's focus test uses `autoFocus: false`.)
- **`preferredSide` (the `minAvailableSpace` flip replacement, `overlay-position-anchored.ts:86-130`) is untested** despite being the most intricate math in the scope — the reset loop's termination, the tie-goes-to-the-initial-side rule and the "never read the pane's own size" invariant all rest on comments alone.
- **Animations are only ~15% covered.** `animated-lifecycle.directive.spec.ts` exercises the settle logic on the leave path only (4 tests). Untested: the enter path, both interrupt paths, `skipNextEnter`, `forceEnteredState`/`forceLeftState` and the `forcedAtFrameId` same-frame skip (the reason the rAF loop exists), the whole of `AnimatableDirective` (batching, parent aggregation, `transitionId` handoff), `AnimatedIfDirective`, and all of `flip-animation.ts`.
- **`overlay-runtime.spec.ts` is good on config surfaces but thin on the async lifecycle.** Most tests (including four of the six close-guard tests and every stacking test) call `ref.close()` while the overlay is still `'mounting'`, taking the synchronous path; nothing covers the enter-frame `interactiveCloseReady` gate, escape handling, or restore-focus-on-close (`restoreFocus` is only tested with the value `false`).
- No spec in scope asserts behaviour believed to be wrong; `overlay-viewport-inset.spec.ts` and `overlay-layer.spec.ts` are small and correct. Worth noting that `reserveOverlayViewportSpace` keeps module-global state, so a spec that forgets its `release()` leaks insets into every later test file in the run.

## theming, providers, props

### High

- **`injectAngularRootElement()` starts an unbounded, uncancellable `setTimeout` poll chain — no `DestroyRef` cleanup, so it outlives the injector.**
  `libs/core/src/lib/providers/angular-root-element.ts:9-20`: `poll()` re-schedules itself every 25 ms until `appRef.components` is non-empty, and nothing ever calls `clearTimeout`. The provider is a `defineRootProvider` with no `destroyRef.onDestroy`. Any environment where a root component never mounts (unit tests, `createApplication()` without bootstrap, injection before bootstrap on the server) polls forever, and `rootElement.set()` would fire against a signal owned by a destroyed injector. Verified at runtime (vitest fake timers): `timers after inject -> 1`, `after 200ms (8 polls) -> 1`, and after `TestBed.resetTestingModule()` + 200 ms still `-> 1` — the chain is still alive with the injector gone. It is also the only provider in the folder with neither a `name` option nor a `provideX` counterpart.

- **The two component CSS files in `libs/core` are the only ones in the repo not wrapped in `@layer components`, which inverts override precedence for every theming token they declare.**
  `libs/core/src/lib/theming/color-interactive-styles.component.css:1` and `surface-interactive-styles.component.css:1` contain no `@layer` at all (verified: `grep -c "@layer"` → 0 for both, while 165/165 `*.component.css` files in `libs/components` are wrapped). AGENTS.md ("Component styling") states the rule unconditionally, and the mechanism it describes bites here concretely: these sheets are injected unlayered via `injectStyleManager().mount(...)`, so their `--et-theme-color-primary-rgb` / `--et-surface-interaction-rgb` declarations beat _any_ rule in `@layer components` regardless of specificity. A component that needs to re-anchor those tokens on the same element that carries `.et-color-interactive` cannot do it from its own (layered) stylesheet without `!important`. Today's consumers escape only because they re-anchor on a _descendant_ (`libs/components/src/lib/forms/rich-text-editor/rich-text-editor.component.css:179-182` targets `.et-rte-content` inside the frame), so inheritance rather than layer precedence resolves it.

## utils, pipes, directives, drag-handle, resize-handles

### High

- **`markdownToHtml` lets an entity-encoded `javascript:` URL through, so its output executes script when bound as HTML.**
  `isSafeUrl` tests the raw string (`libs/core/src/lib/utils/markdown.ts:17-19`) and only strips whitespace/control chars, while `escapeHtmlPreservingEntities` deliberately preserves existing character references (`markdown.ts:9`). The link/image passes then interpolate the unescaped href/src into an attribute (`markdown.ts:139-144`), and the browser decodes the reference at parse time. Verified at runtime: `markdownToHtml('[click](&#106;avascript:alert%281%29)')` → `<p><a href="&#106;avascript:alert%281%29">click</a></p>`, and after `innerHTML` the anchor reports `href = "javascript:alert%281%29"`, `protocol = "javascript:"`. Same for `javascript&colon;…` and for `![x](&#106;avascript:…)` (an `<img src>`), and `java&Tab;script:` also survives. `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:173` claims the opposite ("escapes raw HTML in the Markdown text (so its output is safe to bind as HTML) and refuses script-running URL schemes in links and images"), and `markdown.spec.ts:183-185` only covers the plain-text `javascript:` spelling. `sanitizeInlineHtml`'s `<a href>` passthrough (`markdown.ts:85-89`) has the same hole.

- **`cloneFormGroup` throws on any `FormGroup` that contains a disabled control.**
  `libs/core/src/lib/utils/angular/form.ts:46` calls `clonedForm.setValue(formGroup.value)`, but `FormGroup.value` omits disabled controls while `setValue` requires every key. Verified at runtime with `{ a: enabled, b: disabled }`: `THREW: NG01002: Must supply a value for form control with name: 'b'`. `getRawValue()` (or `patchValue`) is what the code wants. Reachable in shipped code — `libs/cdk/src/lib/components/overlay/components/overlay/filter-overlay.ts:157` clones a consumer-supplied form. `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:60` documents it as deep-cloning "including validators, **disabled state** and nested groups/arrays".

- **`normalizeMatchState` has an inverted round check and never returns `null` for a null match, which silently disables every downstream null guard.**
  `libs/core/src/lib/pipes/ethlete/normalize-match-state.pipe.ts:19` is `else if (match?.round.state !== 'preparing') return MatchStateType.PREPARING_ROUND;` — i.e. `PREPARING_ROUND` is returned when the round is _not_ preparing, and for `null`/`undefined` the optional chain yields `undefined !== 'preparing'` → truthy. Verified at runtime: `normalizeMatchState(null)` → `'preparingRound'`, `normalizeMatchState(undefined)` → `'preparingRound'`, `{ round: { state: 'preparing' } }` → `null`, `{ round: { state: 'started' } }` → `'preparingRound'`. Consequence: the `if (!match || !matchState)` guards in `normalize-match-participants.pipe.ts:39,55` and the state branch in `normalize-match-score.pipe.ts:43-52` can never see `matchState === null` for a real match, and a genuinely preparing round is misclassified.

- **`IsEmail` rejects every address containing an uppercase letter.**
  `libs/core/src/lib/utils/angular/validators.ts:64` uses `/^[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}$/` with no `i` flag. Verified at runtime: `john@example.com` → `null` (valid), `John@example.com` → `{ isEmail: true }`, `john@Example.COM` → `{ isEmail: true }`. Any user who capitalises their name or domain gets an "invalid email" error. `IsEmail(control)` with a non-string value (`42`) also reports invalid rather than being ignored.

### Medium

- **The only component CSS in `libs/core` is not wrapped in `@layer components { … }`.** `libs/core/src/lib/resize-handles/resize-handles.component.ts:103-241` ships an inline `styles:` block with unlayered `et-resize-handles { position: absolute; inset: …; pointer-events: none }` and the `.et-resize-handle--*` rules. `grep -rn "@layer" libs/core/src` returns nothing. Per AGENTS.md ("Wrap every component CSS file in `@layer components { … }`", and "in a `.css` file next to the component") this is exactly the case the rule exists for: a consumer cannot override the handle geometry with a Tailwind utility. No hardcoded colours and no Tailwind in the sheet, so those parts are fine.

- **Both gesture primitives listen on the global `document`, not the element's document — contradicting the documented pop-out guidance.** `libs/core/src/lib/drag-handle/drag-gesture.ts:72-73,89` and `libs/core/src/lib/resize-handles/resize-handles.component.ts:59-60,73` bind `pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel` to the ambient `document`, while `el.ownerDocument` (`drag-gesture.ts:138`) / the injected `doc` (`resize-handles.component.ts:69`) is used only for `suppressTextSelection`. `apps/docs/core/drag-resize.md:95` tells the reader "Pass the document the gesture happens in - not the global one - if the element can live in a pop-up or a portal window", which the primitives themselves do not do: in a popped-out window the gesture would suppress selection in the right document and then never receive a move or a release.

Verified at runtime: `clone(cyclic)` → `THREW: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:174` advertises it as a plain "deep clone (objects, arrays, Map/Set, Date, RegExp, typed arrays)" with no caveat. (Prototype pollution is _not_ an issue — the `key === '__proto__'` branch at `comparison.ts:20` keeps it an own property; verified.)

- **`getCookie` returns `''` for a cookie that does not exist.** `libs/core/src/lib/utils/cookie.ts:17` — `('; ' + document.cookie).split('; name=').pop()?.split(';')[0]` yields `''` when the split does not match, because the prefixed string starts with `;`. Verified at runtime in jsdom: `getCookie('present')` → `"yes"`, `getCookie('definitelyMissing')` → `""`. The declared type is `string | null | undefined`, so callers written against it (`=== undefined`, `?? fallback`, `!== null`) do not detect absence.

- **`*etRepeat` throws on a negative count, and its `linkedSignal` computation performs DOM side effects.** `libs/core/src/lib/directives/repeat.directive.ts:22-48` creates/removes embedded views inside a `linkedSignal` computation, mutates `previous.value` in place (`views.push` / `views.splice`, lines 36 and 43), and needs a dummy `effect` to run at all (line 53). With `count` negative the removal loop calls `viewContainerRef.remove(this.viewContainerRef.length - 1)` on an empty container. Verified at runtime with a signal-bound count: 3 → 5 → 1 works, then `-2` gives `THREW: ASSERTION ERROR: ViewRef index must be positive, got -1`. `numberAttribute` makes `-2` (or `etRepeat="-2"`) type-legal. Side effects in a computed also contradicts the `rxjs-signals`/styleguide rule.

- **`KeyPressManager` reports a repeat on the _third_ press, and models synchronous state with `BehaviorSubject`.** `libs/core/src/lib/utils/key-press-manager.ts:15-16` writes `_isKeyPressed$.next(this._keyPressCount$.value > 1)` _before_ incrementing the count. Verified at runtime: three consecutive `isPressed({keyCode: 8})` calls → `[false, false, true]`. `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:183` says "`isPressed(event)` is `true` from the second press within 100 ms". Also: `_isKeyPressed$`/`_keyPressCount$` are private, never exposed as streams and read via `.value` — pure synchronous state in a `BehaviorSubject`, which `.agents/skills/rxjs-signals/SKILL.md` forbids; and `event.keyCode` (line 12) is deprecated. Consumed for real at `libs/cdk/.../combobox.directive.ts:309,649`.

- **Two wrong MIME strings in `inferMimeType`.** `libs/core/src/lib/pipes/infer-mime-type.pipe.ts:146` returns `'tapplication/vnd.apple.installer+xml'` (leading `t`) and line 74 returns `'image/vdn.microsoft.icon'` (should be `vnd`). Verified at runtime: `.mpkg` → `tapplication/vnd.apple.installer+xml`, `.ico` → `image/vdn.microsoft.icon`.

- **`inferMimeType` mis-parses `fm=` when another query parameter's name ends in `fm`.** `infer-mime-type.pipe.ts:40-48` gates on `queryPart.includes('&fm=')` but then takes `queryPart.indexOf('fm=')`, which matches inside the earlier parameter name. Verified at runtime: `https://x/y.png?wfm=z&fm=avif` → `null` (extension `z`), instead of `image/avif` — and because a bogus `fileExtension` is set, the `.png` fallback is skipped too.

- **`MatchStateType` ships as an _ambient_ `const enum`, which is unusable by consumers compiling with `isolatedModules`.** `libs/core/src/lib/pipes/ethlete/normalize-match-score.pipe.ts:10` declares `export const enum`, and the published types contain `declare const enum MatchStateType` at `dist/libs/core/types/ethlete-core.d.ts:2311`, re-exported at line 3976. Verified with `tsc --isolatedModules`: accessing an ambient const enum member is `error TS2748: Cannot access ambient const enums when 'isolatedModules' is enabled`. `normalizeMatchState`'s return type is that enum, so comparing its result requires the member access. A plain `enum` or a string-literal union would be safe.

- **`createSwipeTracker` locks the gesture to "swiping" on a zero-movement first update.** `libs/core/src/lib/utils/swipe.ts:84-90`: with `positiveMovementY > positiveMovementX` false for `0 > 0`, the `else` branch sets `isSwiping = true`. Verified at runtime: a `mousemove` at the exact start position gives `{isSwiping: true, isScrolling: false}`, and a subsequent clearly-vertical move (dy 200, dx 0) cannot change it. A pointermove with unchanged coordinates is common on touch, and it permanently steals the axis decision from the scroll path.

- **`MustMatch` writes errors onto a sibling control and clears that control's other errors.** `libs/core/src/lib/utils/angular/validators.ts:80,84` call `matchingControl?.setErrors({...})` / `setErrors(null)` from inside a group validator; `setErrors(null)` wipes errors produced by the matching control's _own_ validators (e.g. `required`, `IsEmail`), so a mismatched-then-matched password repeat silently drops them.

- **`createLogger().error` and `.warn` write to `console.log`.** `libs/core/src/lib/utils/logger.ts:14-24` — all three levels route through `writeLog` → `console.log`, so warnings/errors carry no stack, are invisible to console level filters, and are not picked up by error reporting hooked to `console.error`. `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:187` documents `{ log, warn, error }` without saying they are all `log`.

- **The barrel exports a `Validators` symbol that collides with `@angular/forms`.** `libs/core/src/lib/utils/angular/validators.ts:90` → `libs/core/src/index.ts:16`; confirmed present in the published export list (`dist/libs/core/types/ethlete-core.d.ts:3976`). In a component that imports both, one shadows the other silently. `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:62` even calls it "also grouped under the `Validators` const" without flagging the clash.

- **`etScrollObserverStart` / `etScrollObserverEnd` never unregister.** `libs/core/src/lib/directives/scroll-observer-start.directive.ts:11-13` and `-end.directive.ts:11-13` set the sentinel in the host's signal in their constructor with no `DestroyRef` cleanup, and `ScrollObserverDirective` (`scroll-observer.directive.ts:22-23,37-43`) has no clear path, so a sentinel inside an `@if`/`@for` leaves a detached `ElementRef` in `_startEl`/`_endEl` after destruction. (The registration gap is confirmed in source; the resulting `isAtStart`/`isAtEnd` behaviour depends on `signalElementIntersection` and was not verified at runtime.)

### Low

- Doc off-by-one: `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:195` says `createComponentId('et-button')` yields `et-button-1, et-button-2, …`; `libs/core/src/lib/utils/angular/component-id.ts:4-7` starts at `0`. Verified at runtime: `et-scan-0`, `et-scan-1`.
- Comment-policy violations (AGENTS.md "Comments: almost none"): section divider `// --- Nested list helpers … ---` at `libs/core/src/lib/utils/markdown.ts:151`; restating comment `// prefix code with zeros if it's less than 100` at `libs/core/src/lib/utils/runtime-error.ts:22`; `// TODO(TRB): Add correct type once provided by API` with no issue link at `libs/core/src/lib/pipes/ethlete/normalize-game-result-type.pipe.ts:13`; `// Return the score if only one game has been played` restating the `if` above it at `libs/core/src/lib/pipes/ethlete/normalize-match-score.pipe.ts:69`.
- `isSafeUrl` rejects the whole `data:` scheme (`markdown.ts:19`), so `![alt](data:image/png;base64,…)` stays literal text — while `inferMimeType` explicitly supports `data:` URIs. `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:173` describes the rule as refusing "script-running URL schemes".
- `equal(Object.create(null) + {a:1}, {a:1})` → `false` (`comparison.ts:117` requires identical constructors). Verified at runtime. Relevant because `equal` is the documented signal-equality function (`utilities.md:175`) and null-prototype objects come out of `Object.groupBy` and `JSON.parse` reviver patterns.
- `createRxHostListener`/`applyHostListener(s)` type `options` as `EventListenerOptions` (`libs/core/src/lib/utils/angular/host-listener.ts:6,21,28`), so only `capture` is expressible — `passive` and `once` (the reason to pass options on a `pointermove`/`wheel` listener) are type errors.
- Public API hygiene: `_registerStart` / `_registerEnd` (`scroll-observer.directive.ts:37,41`) are underscore-prefixed but public and untagged, and `startGesture` (`drag-handle.directive.ts:82`) / `startResizeGesture` (`resize-handles.component.ts:313`) carry no accessibility modifier despite being template-only entry points.
- `resize-handles.component.ts:99` sets the host class `et-resize-handles`, but the shipped CSS targets the element selector `et-resize-handles` (line 158) — the class is never used by the component's own rules.
- `IsArrayNotEmpty` (`validators.ts:47-54`) returns `null` for any falsy value (including `0`/`''`) and evaluates `.length` on non-arrays, so a numeric control reports `isArrayNotEmpty`.
- `cloneFormGroup` (`form.ts:12-30`) handles `FormArray<FormGroup>` and `FormArray<FormControl>` but a `FormArray` nested inside a `FormArray` is cloned as a `FormControl` holding the array value.
- Barrel/version check clean: every path in `libs/core/src/index.ts` and the sub-barrels resolves, all public symbols in scope appear in the published export lists (including the `ResizeEdge`, `Swipe*`, `Translatable`, `ObjectUrlHandle` types), and `libs/core/src/lib/version.ts:4` (`5.0.0-next.53`) matches `libs/core/package.json`.

Clean: `suppressTextSelection` (`utils/text-selection.ts`) is correct on all the paths constructible — refcounting, double release, restoring a pre-existing inline value — and both gesture primitives release it via `finalize` on end _and_ cancel. `drag-gesture.ts` gets the hard parts right: `pointerId` filtering, `pointercancel` distinguished from `pointerup`, capture failures swallowed for jsdom, the catch-up move at commit, and completion of the stream with the gesture; `DragHandleDirective`'s `exhaustMap` + `share()` + `takeUntilDestroyed()` wiring leaks nothing and the `touch-action` host binding is right. `createObjectUrlHandle`, `createSessionMemory`/`canUseSessionMemory`, `copyToClipboard`/`readFromClipboard` (cold, never erroring, focus restored, SSR-guarded) and `randomId`'s insecure-context fallback are all solid, and `defineProvider` & co. match the documented four-statement/`__PURE__` contract exactly. `getObjectProperty`, `clamp`, `round`, `initials` and `slugify` behave as documented, `markdownToHtml`'s raw-HTML escaping holds for everything except the entity case above, and `RuntimeError`'s `ET<code>` formatting matches the docs.

### Spec coverage

- Well covered: `markdown.ts` (74 assertions incl. round-trips, alignment, nesting, several XSS shapes — but not entity-encoded URLs), `swipe.ts` (11, incl. the trailing-velocity window; no zero-movement axis-lock case), `clipboard.ts` (11, incl. cold-observable and focus restoration), `drag-gesture.ts` (7, incl. cancel-vs-tap and selection release), `text-selection.ts` (4), `object.ts` (7), `slugify`/`initials` (5/6), `object-url` (3), `randomId` (3).
- Zero tests despite carrying logic: `utils/comparison.ts` (`clone`/`equal` — the SDK-wide signal equality function), `utils/math.ts`, `utils/angular/form.ts` (the `cloneFormGroup` crash above would have been caught by one test), `utils/angular/validators.ts` (would have caught the `IsEmail` casing bug), `utils/angular/di.ts` (the whole provider-definition family), `utils/angular/host-listener.ts`, `utils/angular/query-list-changes.ts`, `utils/angular/set-input-signal.ts`, `utils/key-press-manager.ts`, `utils/session-memory.ts`, `utils/logger.ts`, `utils/runtime-error.ts`, and `createComponentId` (only `randomId` is tested in `component-id.spec.ts`).
- All five `pipes/ethlete/*` normalizers are untested — `normalizeMatchState`'s inverted branch survives because nothing exercises it. `to-array`, and the `Pipe` class wrappers generally, are untested (the underlying functions mostly are).
- Directives/components with no spec: `click-outside`, `repeat` (the negative-count crash), the `scroll-observer` trio, `drag-handle.directive.ts`, `resize-handles.component.ts`. Only `restore-scroll.directive.spec.ts` (2 tests) exists.
- `cookie.spec.ts` covers `setCookie` only (2 tests); `getCookie`/`hasCookie`/`deleteCookie`/`getDomain` are untested, which is how the `''`-for-missing behaviour went unnoticed. `infer-mime-type.util.spec.ts` asserts many positive URLs but no unknown/missing-extension or malformed-query cases.
- No spec asserts behaviour judged wrong; `object.spec.ts:118` (`'a.b.e[1'` → `undefined`) passes for an accidental reason (the malformed path parses to index `1`), so it does not actually pin down malformed-path handling.

## seo, app-update, notifications, unsaved-changes

### High

- **Every `apply*Binding` shortcut in `seo/` is dead to signal changes: the wrapper `computed` reads its source inside `untracked`, so it has no dependencies and never recomputes.**
  `head-binding.ts:48-51` (`createPropertyBinding`), `:62` (`createArrayPropertyBinding`), `:74` (`toStringBinding`), plus the same hand-rolled pattern in `meta-binding.ts:323` (`applyKeywordsBinding`), `:348` (`applyRobotsBinding`) and `link-binding.ts:256` (`applyAlternateBinding`). `applyHeadBinding`'s `effect` (`head-binding.ts:28-35`) tracks that empty computed, so neither the update nor the _removal_ path ever runs. Affected public API: `applyDescriptionBinding`, `applyAuthorBinding`, `applyKeywordsBinding`, `applyRobotsBinding`, `applyOgBinding` / `applyOpenGraphBindings`, `applyTwitterCardBindings`, `applyArticleBindings`, `applySocialMediaBindings`, `applyCanonicalBinding`, `applyAlternateBinding(s)`, `applyPrevBinding`, `applyNextBinding`, `applyResourceHintsBindings`. Only the bindings that hand the signal straight to `applyHeadBinding` work (`applyMetaBinding`, `applyLinkBinding`, `applyHeadTitleBinding`, `applyHeadTitleMarker`, `applyStructuredDataBinding`, `applyFaviconOverlay`).
  Verified at runtime: `applyDescriptionBinding(sig)` → `DESC initial: first`, after `sig.set('second')` + `detectChanges()` + `TestBed.tick()` → `DESC after set("second"): first`; after `sig.set(null)` the tag is **still in the document** (`tag present: true`) — i.e. a stale meta tag survives the value going away, and only `destroyRef.onDestroy` cleans up. Same for `applyCanonicalBinding`: `initial: ['https://a.example/']` → after change `['https://a.example/']` (removed correctly only on destroy). This is exactly what the docs promise: `apps/docs/core/seo.md:5` ("Every binding accepts a raw value **or a signal**"), `:154` (the migration example wraps `applyCanonicalBinding` values in signals/computeds), and `meta-binding.docs.mdx:13` / `link-binding.docs.mdx:13` ("**Reactive Updates**: Automatically updates when signal values change").

- **`StructuredDataComponent`'s hand-rolled `</script>` escape is bypassable, so CMS-controlled JSON-LD strings are an XSS sink.**
  `structured-data.component.ts:26` does `JSON.stringify(...).replace(/<\/script>/g, '<\\/script>')` — case-sensitive and whitespace-intolerant — and `:28` feeds the result through `bypassSecurityTrustHtml` into the host's `[innerHTML]` (`:11`). The HTML parser accepts `</SCRIPT >`, `</script\n>` etc., so a name like `safe</SCRIPT ><img src=x onerror=…>` closes the script element early and the rest is parsed as live markup.
  Verified at runtime with `name: 'safe</SCRIPT ><img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'`: `SD child tags: SCRIPT,IMG`, `SD injected img count: 1`, and `SD script json parse: PARSE_FAIL: Unterminated string in JSON at position 73` — the payload escaped the script and became a real `<img onerror>` element (inert in jsdom, live in a browser). The safe technique already exists two files away: `structured-data-binding.ts:59` uses `renderer.setTextContent`, and the comment at `:56-58` even names this component as the one that "has to solve by hand" — the hand-rolled solution is incomplete (`<` escaping, or dropping `innerHTML` entirely, is the fix).

### Medium

- **Array-valued head bindings are snapshot once at call time — a later array can never add, remove or change a tag.** `head-binding.ts:60-67`: `valuesList` is an untracked computed, `forEach` runs synchronously at call time, and each element's `value`/`index` is _captured_ into `computed(() => configBuilder(value, index))`. So `og:image`/`og:video`/`og:audio` arrays (`meta-binding.ts:435-437`), `twitter:image` (`:489`), `article:author`/`article:tag` (`:527-528`) and every `applyResourceHintsBindings` array (`link-binding.ts:289-317`) are fixed forever. Verified: `images` signal `['a.png']` → `['a.png','b.png']`, rendered `og:image` stayed `[ 'a.png' ]`.

- **`injectAppUpdates()` crashes when `provideAppUpdates()` was not called, although the instance is `defineRootProvider`.** `app-updates.ts:107` uses `defineRootProvider` (root factory, per `utils/angular/di.ts:88-92`) but `:96` declares the config with `defineStaticProvider` (no root default) — every other config in scope uses `defineStaticRootProvider`. Verified: `NG0201: No provider found for 'InjectionToken App Updates Config'`. Either the config should be root-defaulted or the instance should be `defineProvider`.

- **A late/async unsaved-changes source reports `hasChanges === true` against a `null` baseline until the capture effect flushes.** `unsaved-changes-tracker.ts:171-181` compares `current` against `_defaultValue()`, which is `null` until the effect at `:161-168` runs. Verified: with `source: signal<FieldTree|null>(null)`, right after `treeSignal.set(tree)` and _before_ `TestBed.tick()`, `guard.hasChanges()` is `true` with `defaultValue: null`; after the tick it is `false`. A `canDeactivate()` / `runCheck()` that lands in that window opens a spurious "discard your changes?" dialog. The existing spec (`unsaved-changes.spec.ts:163-179`) ticks first, so it cannot see this. Cheap guard: `if (defaultValue === null) return false` inside `hasChanges`.

- **Docs contradiction: `flash` does not imply `titleMarker` when `favicon` is set.** `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:99` states "Implies `titleMarker`" unconditionally, but `unsaved-changes-tab.ts:159` only defaults the marker when `flash && !favicon`. `createUnsavedChangesTabLock({ hasChanges, flash: true, favicon: true })` therefore blinks nothing in the title.

- **The build fingerprint compares the live DOM against a pristine document, so one app-appended same-origin `<script src>` makes `isAvailable` permanently `true`.** `app-updates.ts:118` reads `readBuildFingerprint(document)` from the running document at environment-initializer time, while `build-fingerprint.ts:35-37` parses a freshly fetched `index.html`; `readBuildFingerprint` includes _all_ same-origin `script[src]` (`:13-17`). Anything that injects a same-origin script before the initializer (a consent/analytics loader, a polyfill shim) is in one fingerprint and not the other. The comment at `app-updates.ts:116-117` acknowledges drift but the mitigation (reading once) does not address a script already present at read time. Restricting the fingerprint to `<head>` scripts, or intersecting against the fetched document, would close it.

### Low

- `meta-binding.ts:59-138` — ~14 section-divider comments (`// Open Graph - Media`, `// Twitter Card`, `// Book tags (arrays)`, …) inside `DEFAULT_MULTI_INSTANCE_TAGS`; AGENTS.md "Always delete: Section headers and dividers".
- `head-binding.ts:4-8` (`HeadBinding<T>`) and `:79-90` (`createBulkPropertyBinding`, whose `_propertyPrefix` parameter is never used) are exported dead code — no reference anywhere in `libs/` or `apps/`.
- `meta-binding.ts:161-167` — `getSelector` returns `''` for any config without `name`/`property`/`httpEquiv`/`itemprop`/`key` (e.g. the type-legal `applyMetaBinding({ charset: 'utf-8' })`). No crash (Angular's `Meta.getTags('')`/`removeTag('')` short-circuit — verified), but every selector-less binding shares the `''` bucket and dedupes against unrelated tags.
- `link-binding.ts:131` — the link store only removes elements it stamped with `data-link-key`, so a pre-existing `<link rel="canonical">` (index.html, another lib) survives and you get two canonicals; the meta store does the opposite and wipes any pre-existing tag matching the selector (`meta-binding.ts:198-199`), never restoring it. Inconsistent ownership model, and neither behavior is documented.
- `meta-binding.ts:546-552` and `:556-561` — `...config.openGraph` / `...config.twitter` spreads come _after_ the resolved fallbacks, so an explicitly-present-but-`undefined` `openGraph.title` clobbers the `config.title` fallback and no `og:title` is written.
- Promise-based public async surface against `ethlete/no-async-await`'s stated contract ("Every async API in the SDK returns a cold Observable"): `AppUpdates.check: () => Promise<void>` (`app-updates.ts:87,137`), `checkIfDue` (`:147`), `fetchDeployedBuildFingerprint` (`build-fingerprint.ts:27`), `runCheck`/`canDeactivate` (`unsaved-changes-tracker.ts:199`, `unsaved-changes-guard.ts:19`). The rule is disabled in `libs/core/eslint.config.mjs:65-68` with a comment claiming "Two call sites … Floating UI's `Middleware.fn` and the favicon renderer" — that comment is now stale (a comment made wrong by a later change).
- `unsaved-changes-coordinator.ts:28` tags the _exported_ `UnsavedChangesRegistration` type `@internal`, and `:53`/`:89` tag `runCheck`/`register` which are part of the injected coordinator's public shape. `libs/core` has no `stripInternal`, so nothing is actually hidden — just misleading (and `runCheck` is documented as consumer-facing in `apps/docs/core/utilities.md:68`).
- `notifications.ts:253` — a `clickHandlers` entry for a service-worker notification the user dismisses natively is never removed (only `close()` at `:207` clears it); unbounded in a long session.
- `unsaved-changes-tab.ts:101` — `BADGE_HOLDERS` is module-global mutable state; correct per-app in a browser, but it leaks across injectors (tests, multiple bootstraps).
- `structured-data.component.ts:19` — `jsonLD` is public on an exported component although it exists only for the host binding.
- `apps/docs/core/seo.md:3` — "never raw `document` calls" is inaccurate: `link-binding.ts:115,131,145` does `createElement`/`querySelectorAll`/`appendChild` on the injected `DOCUMENT`, and the favicon store additionally uses global `getComputedStyle` (`favicon-binding.ts:25`) and `new Image()` (`:143`).

Clean: the app-update stale-build detection (`stale-build-error.ts`) is a sound message-list matcher with a sensible `ChunkLoadError` fast path; the poll pipeline (`app-updates.ts:216-226`) correctly pauses on hidden, throttles via `minCheckInterval`, and unsubscribes with `takeUntilDestroyed`, and every listener added at `:198-199` is removed on destroy. `fetchDeployedBuildFingerprint` deliberately returns `null` for non-2xx/empty documents, which is what stops an error page from triggering a reload loop, and the `sessionStorage` cooldown genuinely prevents a loop. `notifications.ts` is the strongest file in scope: `destroyed$` instead of `takeUntilDestroyed` (correctly justified for streams that outlive the call), every subscription terminated, both delivery paths guarded by `isClosed` on either side of the async boundary, `getRegistration()` over `ready`, page-only options stripped before the constructor, and permission kept in sync through both the Permissions API and a visibility fallback. The unsaved-changes coordinator's single-flight + abort design is correct and well covered, `abandonAll` releases the tab lock, and the tab lock attaches `beforeunload` only while dirty (bfcache-friendly) with every effect torn down in `destroy()`. The favicon store handles the tainted-canvas, no-2d-context, missing-icon-link and load-race cases explicitly. `applyStructuredDataBinding` writes JSON via `setTextContent`, which is the injection-safe path.

### Spec coverage

- **`seo/` is the gap that let the High findings through.** Only `structured-data-binding.spec.ts` and `favicon-binding.spec.ts` exist — both cover bindings that pass the signal straight through. There is **no spec anywhere in the repo** for `head-binding.ts`, `meta-binding.ts`, `link-binding.ts`, `title-binding.ts` or `StructuredDataComponent` (grep for `applyDescriptionBinding|applyCanonicalBinding|applyOpenGraphBindings|applyHeadTitleBinding|StructuredDataComponent` across `**/*.spec.ts` returns nothing). Minimum additions: a signal-change test per shortcut family, a "value goes null removes the tag" test, the multi-instance/priority dedup rules the docs promise, locale re-transform, and an escaping test for `StructuredDataComponent` with `</SCRIPT >` in a string.
- app-update: good coverage of the chunk-failure matrix, cooldown and `check()`; missing the poll pipeline (visibility gating, `minCheckInterval` throttle), the `NavigationError` route (only `unhandledrejection` is dispatched), and `pollInterval: 0`/SSR paths.
- notifications: thorough (~30 cases across permission, both paths, tags, click relay, autoClose, closeAll, unsupported/SSR). No gap worth calling out.
- unsaved-changes: strong on tracker semantics, all four source kinds, coordinator single-flight/abandon, and the whole tab-lock surface (lock, marker, flash, favicon, badge). Missing: the pre-flush `hasChanges` window above, the `normalizeUnsavedChangesSource` throw path for an unsupported source (`unsaved-changes-source.ts:81`), and `compareFn`.
