## generator: migrate-to-v5

### High

- **The inline-template rewrite uses stale source offsets, so a second `@Component` in the same file gets syntactically mangled.**
  `viewport-service.ts:225-269` iterates decorators of `updatedSourceFileForInline` and splices `updatedContent` using `prop.initializer.getStart()/getEnd()` from that parse — but each splice changes the string length, so every later template is cut at the wrong offset. Verified at runtime: a file with two components (`ACmp`, `BCmp`) came out as `@Component({ selector: 'b-cmp', template'<b>{{ isSm() }}</b>'>' })` — the `:` eaten and a stray `'>'` appended. Uncompilable.

- **Replacement keys are applied as whole-file global regexes, so a `.foo` replacement rewrites the prefix of `.foo$` and produces a syntax error.**
  `viewport-service.ts:128-131` (and the twin at `router-state-service.ts:1333-1336`) does `updatedContent.replace(new RegExp(escapeRegExp(original), 'g'), replacement)` for each entry. `this.vp.isBase` and `this.vp.isBase$` are two separate keys; the shorter one runs first. Verified at runtime, input `base = this.vp.isBase; base$ = this.vp.isBase$;` produced:

  ```
  base = injectIsBase();
  base$ = injectIsBase()$;
  ```

- **`injectIsBase` does not exist in v5 `@ethlete/core`, and `isBase` / `isBase$` map to two different functions.**
  `viewport-service.ts:459` maps `isBase → injectIsBase` for `@ethlete/core`, but `viewport-service.ts:473` maps `isBase$ → 'injectIsLg'` unconditionally (the only entry in `observablePropertyMap` that dropped the ternary). Cross-checked against `libs/core/src/lib/signals/media-queries.ts:14-29`: the exports are `injectIsXs/Sm/Md/Lg/Xl/Is2Xl` — there is no `injectIsBase`. So `isBase` migrates to an unresolvable import, `isBase$` to a different breakpoint.

- **Four of the eight `color-naming` symbol renames, three template attribute renames and two CSS class renames target names that do not exist anywhere in the repo.**
  `color-naming.ts:9-12` renames to `ColoredDirective`, `ColoredStylesComponent`, `SurfacedDirective`, `SurfacedStylesComponent`; `color-naming.ts:25-28` to `[etColored]` / `[etSurfaced]`; `color-naming.ts:39-40` to `.et-colored` / `.et-surfaced`; `color-naming.ts:23-24` to `[etProvideAltColor]`. None of these exist. The real v5 API is `ColorInteractiveDirective` / `[etColorInteractive]` (`libs/core/src/lib/theming/color-interactive.directive.ts:19,24`) and `SurfaceInteractiveDirective` / `[etSurfaceInteractive]` (`surface-interactive.directive.ts:17,22`); the "old" classes were deleted in `af8faf678 fix(core): Remove old theming components and directives`, and no `etProvideAlt*` directive exists at all. The generator renames v4 code to a second dead name and reports `✅ Successfully migrated`.

- **`create-provider` drops `as` aliases and `type` modifiers when it rebuilds an import statement.**
  `create-provider.ts:99` (`otherImports.map((el) => el.name.text)`) and `create-provider.ts:133`/`:1011`-equivalents in the other files rebuild the specifier list from `name.text` only. Verified at runtime:

  ```
  in : import { createProvider, SomeThing as Renamed, type OtherType } from '@ethlete/cdk';
       import { Foo as Bar, type Baz } from '@ethlete/core';
  out: import { Renamed, OtherType } from '@ethlete/cdk';
       import { Bar, Baz, createProvider } from '@ethlete/core';
  ```

  `Renamed`/`Bar` are not exported names — the import no longer resolves, and the `type` modifiers are silently dropped. `viewport-service.ts:1657-1663` and `router-state-service.ts:1011-1017` have the identical defect for the `@ethlete/core` import they extend.

- **The template rewrite `prop` → `prop()` is a bare `\b` word match, so it fires inside HTML comments, static attribute values and attribute _names_.**
  `viewport-service.ts:372` / `:251`. Verified at runtime on one template:

  ```
  <div *ngIf="isXs()">small</div>
  <!-- isXs() mentioned in a comment -->
  <div data-x="isXs()"></div>
  <other-cmp [isXs()]="isXs()"></other-cmp>
  ```

  `[isXs()]="…"` is not a valid Angular binding, and `data-x` was a plain string the migration had no business touching.

- **`[theme]=` → `[color]=` and `[altTheme]=` → `[altColor]=` are applied by blind `replaceAll` to every `.html` and every non-spec `.ts` in the workspace.**
  `color-naming.ts:29-30`, applied at `:141-143` (TS, including string literals) and `:165-167` (HTML). Verified at runtime: `<my-chart [theme]="darkTheme">` — a component that has nothing to do with `@ethlete/core` — became `<my-chart [color]="darkTheme">`, and a TS string literal `'[theme]='` became `'[color]='`. `theme` is an extremely common input name; this is unbounded collateral damage with no report of which files were touched for this reason vs. a real Ethlete binding.

- **`RouterStateService` is matched by identifier name only, so a consumer's own service of that name gets hijacked and its class left uncompilable.**
  `router-state-service.ts:75` / `:96` / `:1149` never check the module specifier (unlike `viewport-service.ts:428-446`, which at least records it). Verified at runtime with `import { RouterStateService } from './my-router-state.service'`:

  ```
  export class A {
    readonly params = injectQueryParams();
    doThing() {
      return this.rs.somethingCustom();   // <- this.rs was deleted
    }
  }
  ```

  The injected property was removed, one member call was rewritten to an unrelated `@ethlete/core` function, and every other call on the same service now references a deleted property.

- **`findClassForRouterStateService` is missing the `if (classNode) return` guard its viewport twin has, so generated members land in the wrong class — and same-named properties in unrelated classes get deleted.**
  Compare `router-state-service.ts:115-138` with `viewport-service.ts:1362` (`function visit(node) { if (classNode) return; … }`); the router version keeps traversing after a hit, so the _last_ matching class wins. `removeRouterStateServiceInjection` (`router-state-service.ts:1044-1070`) then deletes every property named `rs` in every class. Verified at runtime on a file with class `A` (real usage) and class `B` (an unrelated `rs = { queryParams: 1 }`):

  ```
  export class A { go() { return this.queryParams(); } }          // member missing
  export class B { private queryParams = injectQueryParams();     // member landed here
                   go() { return this.queryParams(); } }          // B's own rs deleted
  ```

- **A `monitorViewport()` call is deleted outright, with no replacement and no warning, whenever the workspace happens not to mention `--et-vw`/`--et-sw`.**
  `viewport-service.ts:1520-1534`: if `constructorStatements` is empty the calls are spliced to `''` and the function returns. Verified at runtime — `this.vp.monitorViewport();` in a constructor left `constructor() {\n  }`, the run still printed `✅ Successfully migrated`, and `viewport-service.spec.ts:760` (`'should remove monitorViewport() call'`) encodes this as intended behaviour. The detection itself is workspace-global (`detectCssVariableUsage`, `:310-349`), so the decision for one component is made by whatever any other file in the repo contains.

### Medium

- **`create-provider` only inspects `ts.isImportDeclaration` with named bindings, so three realistic shapes are silently skipped.** Verified at runtime — all three came back byte-identical: `export { createProvider } from '@ethlete/cdk';`, `import { createProvider as cp } from '@ethlete/cdk';` (`create-provider.ts:62` compares `element.name.text`, not `propertyName`), and `import * as cdk from '@ethlete/cdk'; cdk.createProvider()`. Nothing is reported, so the consumer only finds out when the v5 build fails.

- **A host-directive alias written with a space keeps the old public name.** `HOST_DIRECTIVE_REPLACEMENTS` (`color-naming.ts:48-57`) only lists the no-space forms. Verified: `inputs: ['etProvideTheme: theme']` → `inputs: ['etProvideColor: theme']` — the directive input is now `color` but the alias the consumer's templates bind to is still `theme`, and `color-naming.ts:141-143` has already rewritten those templates to `[color]`. Prettier-formatted Angular metadata regularly produces the spaced form.

- **All four sub-migrations skip `.spec.ts`, and the spec asserts this is intentional.** `color-naming.ts:110`, `create-provider.ts:16`, `router-state-service.ts:1256`, `viewport-service.ts:17`; `color-naming.spec.ts:109-116` is titled `'should not modify spec files'`. Consumer test files keep referencing `ViewportService`, `RouterStateService` and `ProvideThemeDirective` — all removed in v5 — so `nx test` breaks after a "successful" migration, and nothing in the output says so.

- **Three of four sub-migrations recurse into `node_modules`, and one of them has no filter at all.** `create-provider.ts:10-23`, `router-state-service.ts:1251-1263` and `viewport-service.ts:12-31` only apply `!path.includes('node_modules')` to the _push_, never to the directory descent. Worse, `detectCssVariableUsage` walks the tree a **second** time (`viewport-service.ts:318-330`) with no filter whatsoever, and its `styleFiles` input (`:19-26`) has no `node_modules` check either — so a `--et-vw` anywhere under `node_modules` flips `hasViewportVariables` for the whole workspace.

- **`findAvailableMemberName` offers `#name` as a candidate, which the emitter prefixes with `private`.** `viewport-service.ts:1404` (`const candidates = [baseName, \`_${baseName}\`, \`#${baseName}\`]`) feeds `:1120` (`private ${member.name} = …`). Verified at runtime on a class that already has `isXs`and`_isXs`: output was `private #isXs = injectIsXs();`plus`this.#isXs()`—`private`on a private identifier is a TS error, and a class that already owns an`isXs` property is exactly the shape this migration targets.

- **The `@ethlete/core` breakpoint remapping is keyed on the literal module specifier, so any re-export path shifts every breakpoint by one.** `viewport-service.ts:449` (`packageName === '@ethlete/core'`) drives `:456-459`, where the non-core branch maps `isLg → injectIsXl`, `isXl → injectIs2Xl`, `isBase → injectIsLg`. A consumer importing `ViewportService` through their own barrel or a tsconfig path alias silently gets the foreign-uikit scale.

- **Import edits use string `.replace()` on whole-file content, which hits the first occurrence anywhere.** `router-state-service.ts:1020`, `viewport-service.ts:1664`, and every `updatedContent.replace(oldText, newText)` in `handleInlineInjectPatterns` (`router-state-service.ts:837,875,923,970`; the viewport equivalent). Two identical expression texts, or an identical import statement, resolve to the wrong site.

- **No scope flag and no report of anything needing manual review.** `schema.json` exposes only `skipFormat` and four on/off toggles; every sub-migration walks the whole workspace from `.`. `libs/core/CHANGELOG.md:657` tells users to "check the console output for warnings about any manual code changes that may be needed", but the only `console.warn` calls in the generator are internal failures (`viewport-service.ts:1105,1216,1593`, `router-state-service.ts:754,1092`) — no transform ever emits a "review this" warning, including the cases above where it knowingly deletes code.

- **Doc mismatch.** `apps/docs/core/index.md:44` lists `injectUrl` among the helpers the generator converts `RouterStateService` to; `injectUrl` appears in no property or method map in `router-state-service.ts:34-61` or `:179-192`, so the generator never emits it. The page also gives no hint that spec files are skipped or that a `monitorViewport()` call can be deleted.

### Low

- Dead code masked by a file-level lint disable: `generateNameFromArgs` (`router-state-service.ts:660`) and `createReplacementsForMember` (`router-state-service.ts:680`) are never called; `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars */` at `router-state-service.ts:1` and `viewport-service.ts:1` is what hides them (along with the unused `original` bindings at `router-state-service.ts:1324` and `viewport-service.ts:118`).
- Comment-policy violations throughout, none of which fit the four allowed cases: narration (`viewport-service.ts:11,35,50,57,60,65,69,103,127,133`, `create-provider.ts:9,53,69,74,98,105,119,126`), trailing meta (`router-state-service.ts:153` `constructorCalls: [], // Initialize`, `:310` `genericType?: string; // Add this`), diff-relative markers (`router-state-service.ts:847` `// NEW: Look for:`), and restatements of the line below (`viewport-service.ts:1565` `// default`, `:1070`).
- Duplicated and inconsistent logging: `migration.ts:25,30,41` prints a bullet, then each sub-migration prints its own banner (`viewport-service.ts:6`, `create-provider.ts:5`, `color-naming.ts:60`, `router-state-service.ts:1247`) — so every step announces itself twice. `migration.ts:33` forgets the bullet for router-state only. `migration.ts` and `router-state-service.ts` use `console.log`, the other two use `@nx/devkit`'s `logger` — so half the output ignores Nx's output settings.

Clean: `formatFiles` is correctly gated behind `skipFormat` and only touches files already changed in the tree, so there is no unconditional-reformat problem here; no dependency is added, so the missing `installPackagesTask` class of bug doesn't apply; `color-naming` is the one walker that correctly prunes `node_modules` directories (`color-naming.ts:108,118`); the template/CSS rewrites use plain `replaceAll` rather than tag regexes, so the "truncate at a `>` inside an attribute value" class doesn't apply; the modification-splicing helpers (`removeViewportServiceInjection`, `migrateMonitorViewport`) correctly sort edits descending before applying; `findMatchingParen` handles nested parens properly; and the emitted names I could check against today's source — `injectRoute/RouterState/RouteData/PathParams/QueryParams/RouteTitle/Fragment/RouterEvent/QueryParamChanges/PathParamChanges/QueryParam/PathParam/RouteDataItem`, `setupScrollRestoration`, `injectObserveBreakpoint`, `injectBreakpointIsMatched`, `injectViewportDimensions`, `injectScrollbarDimensions`, `injectCurrentBreakpoint`, `writeViewportSizeToCssVariables`, `writeScrollbarSizeToCssVariables`, `ProvideColorDirective`, `COLOR_PROVIDER`, `injectColorThemesPrefix`, `createCssColorThemeName`, `.et-color--`/`.et-color-alt--` — all exist.

### Spec coverage

- ~110 cases across four spec files, and the AST-heavy happy paths are covered densely (viewport: toSignal/toObservable combinations, pipe chains, `build()` legacy method, constructor injection, name collisions; router-state: generics, `requireSync`, multiline formatting).
- Every High finding above is uncovered: no spec has two `@Component`s in one file, a `.foo` and `.foo$` usage side by side, a locally-defined `RouterStateService`, two classes in one file, an aliased/`type`/re-exported/namespace import, an unrelated `[theme]` binding, or a template where the property name also appears in a comment/attribute name.
- Three specs encode defects as intended behaviour: `color-naming.spec.ts:34-50` and `:52-68` assert the renames to the nonexistent `ColoredDirective`/`SurfacedDirective`; `color-naming.spec.ts:87-107` asserts `.et-colored`/`.et-surfaced`; `viewport-service.spec.ts:1934` asserts `isBase$ → injectIsLg` while nothing covers plain `isBase` (which resolves to the nonexistent `injectIsBase`); `viewport-service.spec.ts:760` asserts the silent deletion of `monitorViewport()`.
- `migration.spec.ts` is 37 lines and tests only `skipFormat` — the four toggles, their defaults (`!== false`), and any interaction between sub-migrations run on the same tree are untested.
- Nothing asserts on the reported counts or the log output, so a transform that skips a file it claims to have migrated cannot fail a test.
- No spec covers the whole-workspace walk: no case has a `node_modules` fixture, and no case checks that an unrelated file was left byte-identical (only `color-naming.spec.ts:118-126` does that, for a file with no matching content at all).

---

## other generators, packaging, stories

### High

- **`migrate-provider-shape` matches factories by identifier name only and never looks at the module specifier, so a workspace's own helper named `createProvider` / `createLabels` / `createQueryClient` is silently rewritten into code that cannot compile — and the run reports `✓ <file>` / `✅ Rewrote 1 file(s)`.**
  `findTupleSites` keys off `call.expression.text` alone (`provider-shape.ts:99-102`), and `rewriteImports` walks _every_ import declaration and rewrites its named bindings whenever a name is in the table (`provider-shape.ts:184-205`), with `extractorHost` falling back to "any import that names a replaced factory" (`provider-shape.ts:176-182`) — `isCoreImport` (`:227`) is only ever the _second_ preference, never a gate. Verified at runtime against `dist/libs/core/generators/migrate-provider-shape/provider-shape.js`:

  ```
  in:  import { createLabels } from '../i18n/labels';
       export const [provideLabels, injectLabels] = createLabels({ ok: 'OK' });
  out: import { defineLabels, toInjectFn, toProvideFn } from '../i18n/labels';
       const LABELS_DEF = /* @__PURE__ */ defineLabels({ ok: 'OK' });
       export const provideLabels = /* @__PURE__ */ toProvideFn(LABELS_DEF);
  ```

  The local module exports none of those three names. The same path also mis-targets `import { createProvider } from '@ethlete/cdk'` (the v4 location, i.e. exactly the workspaces this codemod is aimed at, before `migrate-to-v5`'s `create-provider` sub-migration has run) — `defineProvider` and the extractors get imported from `@ethlete/cdk`. The migration is scoped to the whole workspace by default (`migration-scope.ts:45-50`), so nothing limits the blast radius.

- **Both tailwind generators derive the `.d.ts` path with `outputPath.replace(/\.css$/, '.d.ts')`, so any `--outputPath` that does not end in `.css` makes the type file overwrite the stylesheet — destroying a pre-existing file, while both writes are logged as successes.**
  `tailwind-4-color-theme/generator.ts:141` writes the CSS, `:147` derives `typesOutputPath`, `:150` writes the `.d.ts`; identical at `tailwind-4-surface-theme/generator.ts:128,134,137`. `.scss` does not match `/\.css$/`. Verified at runtime with `--outputPath=src/styles/theme.scss`:

  ```
  ✅ Generated Tailwind themes at: src/styles/theme.scss
  ✅ Generated color theme name types at: src/styles/theme.scss   ← same path
  ✅ Generation completed successfully!
  files under src/styles: [ 'theme.scss' ]                        ← contains the .d.ts, CSS gone
  ```

  Nothing validates the extension or that the two paths differ. If a user points `--outputPath` at their existing hand-written stylesheet, its contents are replaced by a `declare module` block.

- **`tailwind-4-surface-theme` silently drops a theme's entire `interactionColor` when the swatch is anything other than a fully-populated inline object literal, and still reports `✅ Found 1 surface theme(s)` / `✅ Generation completed successfully!`.**
  `parseInteractionColor` returns `undefined` unless `swatch.color` has all five keys as inline string literals (`tailwind-4-surface-theme/generator.ts:294-311`), and `parseSurfaceThemeObject` only accepts an `ObjectLiteralExpression` initializer for `interactionColor` at all (`:338`). There is no warning on either path. Verified at runtime — with `interactionColor: { color: NEUTRAL_TINT }` (a shared const in the same file, the natural way to give several elevations one tint ladder) and again with a `color` map missing only `disabled`:

  ```
  emits --et-surface-interaction:            false
  emits --color-et-surface-base-interaction: false
  ```

  The generated CSS then carries no `--et-surface-interaction*` at all, so every `[etSurfaceInteractive]` hover/active state and the whole `.et-color--surface` bridge (`:634-656`) fall back to the surface's plain text colour, with the run declared a success. Note the flat-shape guard at `:286-291` _does_ throw a helpful error — it is only reached for inline literals, so the shape most likely to be stale is the one that gets a diagnostic and the shared-const shape is the one that gets silence.

### Medium

- **`migrate-surface-interaction-swatch` has the mirror-image blind spot and no report at all: `interactionColor: SHARED_MAP` is left unmigrated and the run prints `Nothing to migrate.`** `findFlatInteractionColor` requires the initializer to be an `ObjectLiteralExpression` (`interaction-swatch.ts:27`), and `migration.ts:34-38` has no task/report mechanism (unlike its sibling's `PROVIDER_SHAPE_REPORT_PATH`). Verified: `changed: false` for a flat map behind a const reference. The user then hits the surface generator's silent drop above rather than its "run the migration" error. (Spreads _inside_ a literal are handled correctly — verified `{ ...BASE, hover: '1 1 1' }` → `{ color: { ...BASE, hover: '1 1 1' } }`.)

- **`migrate-provider-shape` misses two realistic shapes with zero reporting: an aliased factory import and a re-export.** `collectTasks` only records calls whose callee identifier is itself a known factory name (`provider-shape.ts:288`), and `rewriteImports` only considers `ts.isImportDeclaration` statements (`:173`) — an `ExportDeclaration` is never seen. Verified at runtime, both returned unchanged with an empty task list:

  ```
  import { createProvider as makeProvider } from '@ethlete/core';
  export const [provideX, injectX] = makeProvider(() => 1);      // untouched, unreported

  export { createProvider } from '@ethlete/core';                 // untouched, unreported
  ```

  Both files keep an import of a symbol that no longer exists, and the migration-tasks file says nothing about them.

- **Re-running `migrate-provider-shape` on its own output regenerates `provider-shape-migration-tasks.md` with a spurious task per ref-factory call, telling the user to do what the file already does.** `collectTasks` flags every `createQueryClient` / `createBearerAuthProvider` / `createWebSocketClient` / `createQueryContext` call that is not part of a _tuple_ site (`provider-shape.ts:283-303`), and migrated code by definition has no tuple site left. Verified: pass 2 over pass 1's output returns `changed: false` but one task — "`createQueryClient` returns a provider definition now, not a `[provide, inject, token]` tuple. Read the halves with `toProvideFn` / `toInjectFn` / `toToken`" — pointing at the line that already reads `const QUERY_CLIENT_DEF = createQueryClient(...)` with `toProvideFn(QUERY_CLIENT_DEF)` two lines below. `migration.ts:57-59` writes the report unconditionally whenever `tasks.length > 0`.

- **Overlapping scope flags visit files twice and duplicate every task in the report.** `createMigrationScope` pushes project roots and `--include` prefixes into one un-deduplicated list and loops `visitNotIgnoredFiles` per root (`migration-scope.ts:27-58`), so `--projects=web --include=apps/web` (or `--include=apps --include=apps/web`) visits `apps/web` twice; `migration.ts:48` appends `result.tasks` on each visit. The rewrite itself is idempotent so no double-rewrite, but the report lists each site N times.

- **`devtools-about` wires the _first_ `.ts` file it happens to visit that mentions `provideQueryDevtools(` — spec files included — then stops, leaving the real config untouched and reporting no problem.** `wireProvider` short-circuits on `wired` (`devtools-about/generator.ts:84`) with no filter for `.spec.ts` / `.stories.ts` / test fixtures (`:83-107`). Verified at runtime with a project containing `apps/web/src/app/a-devtools.spec.ts` and `apps/web/src/app/app.config.ts`:

  ```
  a-devtools.spec.ts → import { APP_BUILD_INFO } from '../build-info';
                       ... provideQueryDevtools({ about: APP_BUILD_INFO }) ...
  app.config.ts      → unchanged
  ```

  No warning was printed. The app never reports its build info, and a spec file gained a dependency on a gitignored generated file.

- **Both tailwind generators only resolve `Identifier` elements inside the `THEMES` / `SURFACE_THEMES` array, so inline theme object literals fail with an error that shows the user the shape they already wrote.** `tailwind-4-color-theme/generator.ts:224` and `tailwind-4-surface-theme/generator.ts:203` skip every non-identifier element; the empty-result throw at `:259` / `:240` then surfaces as `No valid surface themes found in SURFACE_THEMES array` followed by the hint `export const SURFACE_THEMES = [...] satisfies SurfaceTheme[];`. Verified at runtime. Same class: a swatch map given as an identifier (`color: BRAND`) or spread from an **imported** const drops the whole theme with a `⚠️ Failed to parse theme brand: ThemeSwatch must have color and onColor properties` warning and then hard-fails — `parseColorMap` only resolves spreads against variable declarations in the _same_ source file (`tailwind-4-color-theme/generator.ts:440`) and returns `null` for a bare identifier initializer (`:419-484`). Both verified. `apps/docs/core/theming.md:15-33` never documents the "one exported const per theme, referenced by identifier, colour maps inline" constraint that the parsers actually impose.

- **`libs/core` publishes `vite` and `@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular` as exact-pinned peers purely because `vite.config.mts` is not in the `@nx/dependency-checks` ignore list.** `libs/core/eslint.config.mjs:11` sets `ignoredFiles: ['{projectRoot}/eslint.config.{js,cjs,mjs,ts,cts,mts}']` only, while `libs/components/eslint.config.mjs:13-17` also ignores `'{projectRoot}/vite.config.{js,cjs,mjs,ts,mts}'`. Confirmed the only importers in `libs/core` are `vite.config.mts` (build tooling) and `src/test-setup.ts`; `libs/components/package.json` correspondingly has neither in its peers. Result: `libs/core/package.json:7,19` ship `"@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular": "2.6.3"` and `"vite": "8.1.5"` as (optional) peers of a runtime library. They are optional so nothing installs, but an exact pin on `vite` will produce peer-conflict noise for any consumer not on vite 8.1.5. `typescript: "6.0.3"` and `ts-morph: "21.0.1"` (`:17-18`) are legitimately generator-driven but likewise exact-pinned.

- **`apps/docs/core/index.md` "Nx generators" bullet lists only the two tailwind generators, omitting two of the six shipped generators.** `libs/core/generators/generators.json` registers `migrate-surface-interaction-swatch` and `devtools-about`, neither of which appears in the core overview's generator list (`apps/docs/core/index.md`, "Also in the package"). Both _are_ documented elsewhere (`apps/docs/core/theming.md:78`, `apps/docs/query-devtools/index.md:1771`), so this is an index gap, not undocumented API.

The region label `//#region Migration main` (`:55`) is also wrong — it is a generator, not a migration.
- Dead parameters and dead locals in `tailwind-4-color-theme/generator.ts`: `addSpacingBefore` is `false` at all three call sites (`:601,605,609` vs `:687-691`); `altPrefix` is `''` at its only call site (`:632` vs `:772`); `outputDir` is computed only to log (`:136-139`); `defaultThemes`/`regularThemes`/`mainThemes` (`:544-545,590`) just reorder the same array before a `.some()` over all of it.
- `generators/tsconfig.json` sets `"declaration": true` and emits `.js.map` sourcemaps, neither of which is in `ng-package.json`'s asset globs — so `dist/libs/core/generators/**/*.js` ships with a dangling `//# sourceMappingURL=…` (confirmed at the tail of `dist/libs/core/generators/migrate-provider-shape/provider-shape.js`) and the `.d.ts` output is generated and discarded.
- `generators.json` uses the legacy `"factory"` key rather than `"implementation"` for all six entries and carries no `$schema` / `name` / `version`. Nx normalises `factory` → `implementation` (`nx/dist/src/command-line/generate/generator-utils.js`), so it works.
- `libs/core/src/lib/stories/changelog-page.mdx:3` names the imported CHANGELOG `Readme`.

Clean: the published package is correct. `NX_NO_CLOUD=true npx nx build core` succeeds and `dist/libs/core/generators/` contains all six generator directories with their `.js` implementations, `schema.json` files and `generators.json`, matching the `"generators": "./generators/generators.json"` field in `dist/libs/core/package.json`. `build`'s `dependsOn` covers `build-generators`, which is uncached (`nx:run-commands`, no `targetDefaults` entry) so it always reruns, and `libs/core/generators/**/*.ts` is inside the `production` named input (`nx.json`), so a generator edit correctly invalidates the `build` cache. The generators emit ESM (`module: preserve`) into a `"type": "module"` package, which is consistent; loading them through Nx's actual loader path (`require()` on Node 24) resolves — relative imports carry explicit `.js` extensions throughout, and the `exports` map's omission of `./generators/*` is harmless because Nx joins `dirname(packageJsonPath)` with the `generators` value on the filesystem rather than resolving a subpath. `sideEffects: false` is safe: the only bare imports in `libs/core/src` are in `test-setup.ts`, and the two theming `.component.css` files reach the bundle through `styleUrl`, not a side-effect import. `README.md` is accurate — every symbol in its example and every docs URL it links resolves. `libs/core/src/lib/stories/` holds only `changelog-page.mdx`, which is picked up by `apps/storybook/.storybook/main.ts`'s `../../../libs/**/*-page.mdx` glob and points at the right CHANGELOG. `nx lint core`, `nx test core` and `nx build core` all pass.

### Spec coverage

- `migrate-provider-shape/provider-shape.spec.ts` (10 cases) covers only well-behaved `@ethlete/core` imports. Nothing asserts the module specifier is respected, nothing feeds the codemod its own output (idempotence), and nothing covers an aliased import or a re-export — the three confirmed defects above.
- `migrate-surface-interaction-swatch/interaction-swatch.spec.ts` (5 cases) has good idempotence coverage (`leaves an already migrated swatch alone`, `leaves a swatch that already carries onColor alone`) but no case for `interactionColor` behind an identifier or a function call, i.e. the shape it silently skips.
- `tailwind-4-surface-theme/generator.spec.ts` covers the flat-map → migration-pointer error (`points at the migration when a theme still uses the flat map`) but never asserts that a _malformed swatch_ is reported rather than dropped, and never uses a shared tint const. No case for inline theme literals in the array.
- `tailwind-4-color-theme/generator.spec.ts` (820 lines) covers spreads of same-file consts (`should handle complex spread operations`) but not identifier-valued colour maps, imported spreads, or inline theme literals. No case pins `outputPath` / `typesOutputPath` collision — both generators have `should honor a custom typesOutputPath` tests that only ever pass `.css`/`.d.ts` pairs.
- `devtools-about/generator.spec.ts` has exactly one file containing `provideQueryDevtools()` in every case, so first-file-wins is never exercised; no case re-runs the generator to pin the already-wired path.
- `migration-scope.ts` has no spec of its own, so overlapping `--projects`/`--include` roots and the resulting duplicated tasks are untested.

---

## Cross-cutting themes

1. **The bugs live where the specs are not.** About two thirds of the non-spec source has zero tests: `seo/` bindings, `props/` (490 lines, also zero consumers), `provide-color.directive.ts`, `breakpoint-input.ts`, `scrolling/`, `overlay-focus.ts`, all five `pipes/ethlete/*` normalizers, `validators.ts`, `comparison.ts`, `breakpoint-observer.ts`. Nearly every High finding sits in an untested file, and most would fall to a five-line table test. The test setup itself blocks part of this: jsdom with no `ResizeObserver`/`IntersectionObserver` polyfill makes the element helpers untestable as written.
2. **Docs that promise what the code does not do.** The scan found doc/code contradictions in most domains: "SSR-safe" element signals that construct observers eagerly, SEO bindings sold as reactive, `flash` "implies `titleMarker`", `markdownToHtml` "refuses script-running URL schemes", the renderer "keeps DOM writes SSR-safe", "no built-in reduced-motion handling" (there is), semantic-theme injectors that "throw a friendly error" (dead code), and signature/enum mismatches in the overlay page. A docs-verification pass against runtime behavior would pay for itself.
3. **Generators rewrite by name, not by provenance.** `migrate-to-v5` (RouterStateService, `[theme]`), `migrate-provider-shape` (factory identifiers), and `devtools-about` (first file wins) all match bare identifiers or strings with no module-specifier gate, default to whole-workspace scope, and print `✅` regardless. The verified damage ranges from uncompilable output to silent collateral rewrites of unrelated code. Any fix should start with one shared rule: a rename fires only when the symbol demonstrably comes from the `@ethlete/*` package being migrated, and everything skipped gets a report line.
4. **Migration targets that do not exist.** `migrate-to-v5` renames v4 theming symbols to `ColoredDirective`/`[etColored]`/`.et-colored` and `isBase` to `injectIsBase` — none of which exist in v5. Specs assert these renames, so the suite locks the wrong names in. Every emitted name in every generator should be cross-checked against the current `libs/core/src` exports (most others do check out).
5. **One-shot latches and module-global state break the second instance.** `capturedDefault` in the breakpoint transforms, the `hasWritten*` flags in `css-vars.ts`, `BADGE_HOLDERS`, the overlay root wipe-on-first-mount, the viewport-reservation registry, and `history.scrollRestoration` left on `'manual'` all assume exactly one app per document and one lifetime per module load. HMR, tests, Storybook docs pages and micro-frontends all violate that assumption.
6. **Cleanup gaps cluster around timers and observers, not subscriptions.** RxJS hygiene is consistently good (`takeUntilDestroyed` everywhere), but raw `requestAnimationFrame`/`setTimeout` loops leak in four places (`AnimatedLifecycleDirective`, `signalAnimatedNumber`, `injectAngularRootElement`, the pending scroll restore), and the scrollbar-ruler `<div>` and scroll-observer sentinels outlive their owners.
7. **The `@layer components` rule stops at the lib boundary.** All 165 component CSS files in `libs/components` are wrapped; the three shipped stylesheets in `libs/core` are not. Since core's sheets carry the theming tokens themselves, the omission is worse here than it would be anywhere else.
8. **Dead public surface.** The entire `props/` module, `HeadBinding`/`createBulkPropertyBinding`, `booleanBreakpointAttribute`/`numberBreakpointAttribute`, surface `syncWithProvider`, `debounceFirst`, `skipFirstRun` + `skipSyncRead`, `InjectUtilConfig.injector`, and `setInnerHTML` are exported, mostly documented or half-documented, and consumed by nothing. Each is either a removal candidate or a missing feature; leaving them ships bugs nobody exercises.
9. **`@internal` is aspirational in core.** `libs/core` has no `stripInternal`, yet the tag sits both on API that other libs import (`forceColor`, `resolveAppRootColorProvider`) and on API documented as consumer-facing (`runCheck`), while genuinely internal mutators on `OverlayRuntimeRef` (`finishClose`, `markOpened`) carry no tag at all. Decide the mechanism first, then re-audit the tags.
